title: Opening of Zaki Nassif Museum
summary: Grand opening of Zaki Nassif Museum and Music School of APSAD in Mashghara, West BekaaZaki Nassif Museum which will serve also as Music School of APSAD, was officially inaugurated on May 21, 2016 in Mashghara Western Bekaa by their…
content:
Grand opening of Zaki Nassif Museum and Music School of APSAD in Mashghara, West Bekaa

Zaki Nassif Museum which will serve also as Music School of APSAD, was officially inaugurated on May 21, 2016 in Mashghara Western Bekaa by their Excellences’ the Minister of Culture, Raymond Araiji (represented by M. Sarkis Khoury) and the Minister of Tourism Michel Pharaon. A number of officials, and high-profile figures attended the opening ceremony held on the site of the Museum.

After a tour of the site, The President of the Association for The Protection of Natural Sites and Old Buildings in Lebanon (APSAD), Mrs. Raya Daouk, thanked all who contributed to transform this house into Zaki Nassif Museum. She hoped that this achievement constitutes a model for other similar ones that would honor creative Lebanese personalities that gave Lebanon successes in socio-cultural sectors.

The representative of Zaki Nassif’s Family,

Dr. Nabil Nassif thanked also all those who contributed to preserve Zaki Nassif’s legacy, first the American University of Beirut and of course the APSAD that has just achieved the dream of the artist's sisters and brothers in transforming this house into a Museum and a School.

Mr. Sarkiss Khoury, representative of Araiji, thanked APSAD for the restoration of this house and its transformation to a Museum and a Cultural Center. This has proven to the public opinion that “musical heritages are no less significant and important than architectural heritages.”

In his word, Pharaon expressed his emotion saying: "when we entered this house I felt like Zaki is present, and I imagined if he was still alive, now 100 years old sitting on the couch with my 115 years old uncle Henry pharaon, chating about the history of Lebanon and the glorious Bekaa where they lived, and where we will live in.”

Finally, Dr. Daoud Saigh declared Mrs.Daouk “an honorary citizen of Mashgahra.”

The inauguration ceremony was ended by a concert performed by the Conservatoire’s Lebanese Oriental Orchestra under the baton of Maestro Andre Hajj.

content:
توقيع إتفاق تعاون لإنشاء مدرسة للموسيقى

في متحف ومركز زكي ناصيف الثقافي في مشغرة

أقامت جمعية الأبساد مساء السبت 19 كانون الأول 2015 في قصر إنطوان مقبل "اسكندر سرسق سابقًا"،حفل توقيع "إتفاقية تعاون" بين كل من الأبساد، ووزارة الثقافة، والجمعية اللبنانية لتطوير الموسيقى الأوركسترالية (LeBAM)، والمعهد الوطني العالي للموسيقى، ومدرسة شنلر في البقاع الغربي، من أجل إنشاء مدرسة للموسيقى في متحف ومركز زكي ناصيف الثقافي في مشغرة، وقد حضر الحفل العديد من الشخصيات السياسية والإجتماعية.

وفي المناسبة، ألقت رئيسة الجمعية السيدة ريا الداعوق كلمة رحبت فيها بالحضور، وشكرت كافة الاطراف المعنية ب "إتفاقية التعاون" على ما أبدوه من استعداد لإنجاح مشروع إنشاء هذة المدرسة الموسيقية التي سيستفيد منها كافة أطفال المنطقة. (كلمة السيدة داعوق)

كما ذكّرت السيدة داعوق بالإتفاقية التي وقعتها في كانون الأول 2014 مع مؤسسة فاكتوم العالمية بالتعاون مع وزارة الثقافة اللبنانية بهدف توثيق المعالم الأثرية عبر تصويرها بتقنية عالية الجودة وثلاثية الأبعاد، تَرفَعُ أَدقَّ تفاصيلِها، بهدفِ حُفظها للأجيالِ المقبلة، ولِتُشكِلَ الوثيقةَ التفصيلية والدقيقة لمطلقِ أَي عملية ترميم قد تحتاجها هذه المواقع. وقد تم عرض وثائقي قصير عن كيفية عمل هذه التقنية وعن توثيق "النصب الأشوري في نهر الكلب" الذي يعود لأكثر من الف سنه قبل الميلاد.

في الختام، أحيت الفنانة الشابة فايا يونان حفل موسيقى تحت عنوان "فايا يونان تغني تراثنا" تمييز بعذوبة صوتها وأدائها الفريد.

content:
APSAD kesrwan – Jbeil
"Journée Patrimoine MTEIN "
22-5-2014

Jeudi 22 mai, c’est par une belle journée toute ensoleillée - contrairement aux prévisions de la météo de la veille – qu’une soixantaine de personnes – un groupe homogène et enthousiaste répond à l’appel de l’APSAD, fidèle à sa mission d’organiser avec le ministère de la culture des journées de sensibilisation au patrimoine Libanais. Cette année l’APSAD Kesrwan-Jbeil a fixé son choix sur Mtein.
Après un parcours de route magnifiquement bordée de bosquets de pins vert scintillant de lumière, de chênes centenaires et les incontournables genêts dorés du mois de mai, nous arrivons à la place de Mtein appelée " Al-Midan ".
" Les origines de Mtein, le petit-Metn, paraissent remonter aux premiers siècles de l’ère Chrétienne, ce que semblent prouver les vestiges d’une nécropole rupestre Romano-Byzantine dans les environs… " Quant à son histoire moderne elle commence au 16eme et 17eme siècle lorsque les Muqaddamine ou chefs du clan Abillama s’y établissent. Ces derniers étaient de religion druze avant de passer au Christianisme. Mtein allait connaître alors un véritable âge d’or durant le 18eme et 19eme siècle. De cette belle époque, Mtein - dans son large ensemble s’élargit de 54 millions de km2 - conserve trois demeures patriciennes donnant sur cette majestueuse place où se déroulaient jadis les festivités et les spectacles. A l’Est un palais avec son charmant Mandaloun en bois dentellé et coloré orne cette place, et à l’Ouest, où notre visite va débuter, se trouve la municipalité de Mtein - ancien Palais de Justice.
Un chaleureux accueil nous attend à la municipalité, où son Président Monsieur Zouheir Bounader et Monsieur Selim Abou-Rizk architecte urbaniste membre du conseil, nous explique. " Cette belle bâtisse de style traditionnel libanais se démarque par sa façade très sobre. Son beau portail où alternent les pierres blanches et jaunes est surmonté d’une double arcature comportant deux bans latéraux. Quant à l’étage, il est percé de trois baies surmontées d’arcs surbaissés, caractéristiques de l’architecture du 17eme et 18eme siècle. Le balcon à fleurs est soutenu par neufs corbeaux ". "Ce bâtiment a été presque entièrement détruit et brûlé durant les attaques meurtrières de la guerre puis entièrement reconstruit avec son auditorium, son musée, grâce à la bonne volonté, ténacité et générosité des habitants, spécialement celle de Monsieur Roger Sarrouf évoquée souvent en reconnaissance de ces nombreuses donations
Les murs du musée sont entièrement tapissés de remarquables toiles offertes d’un même élan de solidarité par certains de nos meilleurs artistes peintres libanais. Et c’est par une traditionnelle pause-café offerte par nos hôtes de la municipalité que nous terminons cette visite si enrichissante.
2e visite
A flanc de colline un édicule cubique coiffé d’une coupole, une Qoubbah, recouvrant les sépultures des " Muqaddamine " druzes de la dynastie des Abillama certifie encore de leur ancienne présence.

3e visite
L’ancien beau palais typique de la famille El Akl, heureusement, en voie de restauration.

4e visite
Les magnaneries, anciens vestiges des années d’or de Mtein.

5e visite
La production d’arak et de vin chez les familles : Abou-Nader qui ont tenu à offrir de leur bon vin a tous les invités ; et Abou-Sleiman qui nous avait préparé un cocktail dégustation très bien accueilli. Cette production qui remplace celle de la soie est une heureuse initiative lucrative pour la main -d’œuvre du village.

6e visite
Musée en voie de réorganisation de l’illustre peintre natif de Mtein Georges Khairallah décédé malheureusement dans ses 33 printemps laissant un important héritage de chefs- d’œuvre : peintures, sanguines, fusains et huiles.

7e visite
"Notre Dame de Mtein" l’une des six églises du village, bel édifice tout en pierres d’époque appartenant à la famille Akl.

8e visite
L’ancien palais du 18eme siècle de kabalan Abillama acheté et en voie de réparation par maître Fayçal Al Kantar. Actuellement foyer et restaurant où un déjeuner qui "sent bon le terroir" nous est copieusement servi. Ce fut un bon moment de détente dans ce cadre de pure tradition Libanaise.

L’équipe de l’APSAD Kesrwan-Jbeil composé ce jour-là de Maritta Frem, Mona Yazbek, Dolly Khawam et tous les participants saluons les efforts conjugués de Chaké et Ghassan, du Comité de la Municipalité de Mtein spécialement de son dynamique Président Monsieur Zouhair Abou-Nader de Monsieur Sélim Abou-Rizk infatigable ne tarissant pas d’explications sur son beau village !
Avec cette bonne volonté de garder, de protéger, de développer et de faire aimer son patrimoine notre Liban vivra-t-il encore des années d’or ?

Comité Kesrwan- Jbeil

content:
APSAD Heritage Day 2014

APSAD faithful to its mission of raising awareness of the Lebanese heritage organized 2 guided visits on this occasion the first one on may 13 to Tannourine and Chatine the second on may 15 to Jezzine and Bkassine.

Chatine – Tannourine
This first day proved to be an ecological event. We were invited by the Younes family who were restoring two houses in this region.

Architect Hala Younes told us that those houses were being restored in the greatest respect of traditional techniques with the use of old materials and recovery (earth, lime, clay, straw, wood and stone). This house is going to be a Cultural center and an artist’s residence.

This original initiative encouraged already other inhabitants, since the owner of the neighboring house proposes to open a guest house which will host the future visitors of the Cultural center.

After visiting those houses we were escorted to the beautiful garden of Rania, the sister of Hala, agronomist engineer, to enjoy the products of the soil. In a dream atmosphere, we received a very warm reception for lunch, with unlimited generosity.

We went to the village of Ballouh Baatura, or The Three Bridges Chasm in Balaa.
The lighting in the village is already solar.
Some five minutes away from the village into the valley below, one stops, with bated breath, before the fantastic panorama presenting itself to one's eyes: three natural bridges, rising one above the other over a height of one hundred meters and overhanging the enormous mouth of a chasm plunging 250 meters deep into the bowels of Mount Lebanon! During the months of March and April, when the snows are melting, one sees a mighty 100-metre cascade which thunders and roars behind the three bridges before being swallowed up in the earth.

Then the cars drove us to Tannourine. Historical refuge of Christian populations, Tannourine today counts 40 ancient churches, convents and monasteries, including the visited church of Mar Challita in the center of the village, dating back to the 18th century and the monastery of St. Anthony of Wata Houb.

Members of Tannourine municipality and Vice-president Mr. Nehmé Harb, were greately happy in receiving and showing us the relics of the past in the village.
Visitors were then invited to have coffee in the halls of the newly restored municipality building.

Then we had a walk in the Reserve of Tannourine Cedars rich of 1, 5 million trees, which became an observation of fauna and flora Centre.
On the way back, one last stop to refresh with traditional lemonade at Batroun, before heading to the Noisy and crowded city…

Excellent trip! True Heritage Day…

Jezzine – Bkassine

The second Heritage day takes place in southern Lebanon. In climbing the mountain road from Saida, we can see the cliff of Jezzine, a waterfall and houses overlooking the vast forest of pine Bkassine. We see in the distance the rocky site Niha, refuge of the Emir Fakhreddine II during his escape from the Ottomans. Known as cave Fakhreddine it is rather his father’s Emir Korkmaz.

At Jezzine, hosted by MP André Wazir, Vice President of the Municipal Council, we strolled through the streets to watch an old water mill and old houses. The recently renovated traditional souk offering many shops, the famous cutlery, local crafts from the 18th century.

The Kanaan family receives us in his large house near the municipality. In this house, small children of Kanaan talk about their grandfather, independence hero who also participated in the design of the Lebanese flag. In front of family portraits and a collection of rifles a whole of Lebanon's history is unfolding before our eyes...

Visit of the Serhal palace, perched on a hill, a gigantic mansion; we admired wall sculptures amazing mixture of Ottoman styles, Andalusian, gothic, Hindu, Moorish ... The unfinished and abandoned dream of Dr. Farid Serhal, doctor, artist and visionary...

Finally, it is the turn of Mr Habib Fares, President of Bkassine Municipality, to welcome us at the place of the impressive church of Mar Tacla newly renovated.

After visiting the church and an old house a picnic lunch was offered to the visitors at the beautiful sunny park of Bkassine. We have no word to explain our gratitude to these gentle people.

We ended the tour with a walk through the pine forest of Bkassine, the largest in the Middle East, in which an eco-tourism project is about to emerge: the Forest House, comprises bungalows and a center for visitors.

We conclude these two Heritage Days with the conviction that in order to love and protect your heritage you have first to know it.

title: ROTARY lunch - conference
summary: On January 27, 2014 Rotary Club Beirut Cedars organized a lunch-conference at the Palm Beach Hotel.Mr Nabil Abboud member of the Rotary Club committee has invited from the committee of APSAD President Raya Daouk for talk about APSAD works…
content:
On January 27, 2014 Rotary Club Beirut Cedars organized a lunch-conference at the Palm Beach Hotel.

Mr Nabil Abboud member of the Rotary Club committee has invited from the committee of APSAD President Raya Daouk for talk about APSAD works and projects.

Were present to this conference from our committee Asma Freiha, Maritta Frem, Nina Tabourian and Robert Wehbé.

There was a video presentation on screen of all APSAD’s activities included it’s actual and future projects :

-ZN Museum already started
-Restoration of Baabda palace
-Restoration of APSAD’s office in Deir el Kamar

On this occasion APSAD President Raya Daouk made a speech in French; she spoke of heritage.

Pourquoi le Patrimoine ?

Dans un pays mutilé par les guerres successives ; nous avons fait un choix : avoir notre enfer plutôt que le paradis des autres…et nous sommes ici !

Avec notre choix : nous avons des rêves …qui font partie de la vie : c’est un besoin …Sans rêves pas de réalisations.

Nos rêves c’est aussi d’avoir un pays qui nous cadre, qui nous reflète : non seulement dans le malheur des guerres, mais dans la beauté de l’âme, de la vie et dans le souvenir des générations passées et l’espoir d’un bel avenir.

Le relâchement nous submerge de partout : entre la jungle du béton et l’urbanisation sauvage de nos villages qui jadis, reflétaient une certaine beauté sereine, notre quotidien se détériore à vue d’œil…Notre loyauté envers notre pays devrait faire unir nos efforts pour essayer de sauvegarder ce qui fut la fierté de nos ancêtres et de restaurer et construire dans la beauté, ce qui sera le patrimoine de nos enfants.

La beauté n’est pas le luxe des sociétés aisées : C’est une noble facette d’un bel esprit …et l’esprit n’a ni prix, ni dimension.

Cet esprit qui sait capter les petites lueurs et peut les valoriser, n’étouffera guère par l’obscurité !

A nous de penser , de lutter pour mieux agir ensemble ; car bien bâtir , c’est semer la graine qui va devenir l’arbre grandiose de notre lendemain !

Nous nous le devons, nous le devons à nos enfants.

Permettez-moi de vous présenter notre association, l’APSAD, de façon concise et concrète, notre vision et nos réalisations.

Merci de votre attention.

Raya Daouk
Présidente de l’APSAD

title: National Built Heritage
summary: The Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities (SCTA) had organized the third Annual National Built Heritage Forum in Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah. It was held under the patronage of HRH Prince Faisal bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, governing…
content:
The Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities (SCTA) had organized the third Annual National Built Heritage Forum in Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah. It was held under the patronage of HRH Prince Faisal bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, governing prince of Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah Province. It was held in cooperation with Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah Emirate, Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah Regional Municipality, Taibah University and other government and private associations.

APSAD was the sole organization from outside who joined this special event, which was held at Taibah University during the period of 8-12/12/2013.

Here below a report of the event from APSAD.

APSAD Report

The National Built Heritage Forum 2013 The forum opened with a speech from His Royal Highness Prince Sultan bin Salman bin Abdul Aziz. In this the agenda for the forum and the SCTA was outlined. HRH Prince Sultan talked at length about the need to consolidate and revive Saudi culture. It was apparent that the guests at the forum were there to make presentations but also to coordinate with Saudi construction companies in order to find ways of developing pre-existing heritage sites. This was also done with a view to conserving what may remain in a way that celebrates and preserves the integrity of the area. It is the construction companies within Saudi that are lobbied for the funding of conservation and development projects. There is a clear intent to open up the country to tourism and to consolidate existing heritage sites.
List of topics at the Forum:
 The current issues related to the built heritage in the Kingdom, in general, and in Al-Madinah, in particular:

I. Highlighting the built heritage sites in Al-Madinah Province.
II. The cultural and aesthetic value of the urban heritage in the Kingdom, namely in Al-Madinah.

 Stories about the built heritage sites in the Kingdom.

 Role of urban heritage in creating the national identity. The role of urban heritage in building up national identity.

 Role of municipalities in the preservation of built heritage and means of its development.

 Maintaining the traditional architecture style in housing and architectural projects at the provinces (municipalities’ excellent experiences in this domain).

The higher education in the urban heritage field:

I. Evaluating the status of the higher education in the field of built heritage.
II. The relation between heritage and practicing contemporary architecture in the Kingdom.
III. Role of public and private bodies in training the specialists and local community in the field of heritage building rehabilitation and restoration.

Role of the local community in developing the urban heritage:

I. Social awareness of the built heritage value and its impact on the preservation.
II. Fields of the local community’s participation in the preservation and investment of built heritage.

 Woman’s role in the built heritage.

 Rehabilitation and investment in the field of built heritage and its development.

 Successful experiences in the investment in the built heritage development and employing such experiences economically.

 Financing the built heritage projects.

 Local and international experiences in financing the preservation and rehabilitation of urban heritage.

(taken from the forum website: http://www.nbhf.org.sa/english/NewsIndexEn.aspx)

The opening speech by HRH Prince Sultan celebrated Saudi pre and post Islamic culture and awarded students with prizes for projects in Architecture and Conservation.

APSAD was provided with a booth where projects were presented. The itinerary for the week consisted of attending lectures and presentation in the conference hall for 5 days, from Sunday to Thursday, and presenting APSAD’s projects in the presentation space.

In Prince Sultan’s speech there were tentative public statements aimed towards celebrating pre Islamic heritage, really although the speech sort of navigated around this, there is a huge investment going into places like Mada’in Saleh. The Prince raises the funds mainly from large construction companies like El-Seif and the Bin Laden group. The speech was about three hours long and ranged from discussing a move away from total reliance on oil and a celebration of Islamic heritage. The media here seems to really be pushing at opening the country to skilled expats and creating a Saudi base of knowledge, where Saudis are learning from whomever they may need to with a view to implementing the skills themselves. This section, on education, was one where the fact that the conference was being held in Taybar University became more pertinent.

Guests were invited on Monday to La-Ula for a concert and performance of traditional music and popular folk poetic recitals and later hosted for dinner nearby. The event was enjoined ‘…with the participation of 100 researchers, administrators and specialists in the field of architectural heritage from inside and outside the Kingdom, along with a wide participation of the local community in Madina, Al-Ula and Yanbu.’

The site of La-Ula has been restored to show what a traditional Saudi village would have been like. The houses were faithfully restored and a tour was held where the guide explained what daily life within the village would have been like until quite recently. On Tuesday a trip to Yamboh was organized where the guests were taken on a tour of the renovated port town, where again houses had been restored and a performance of dance and song was arranged. At the finale of the show a traditional Saudi sword dance was performed and the guests were invited to join in.

On the Wednesday guests were taken to the site of Mada’in Saleh where a quick tour of the site underwent hosted by Dr Hussein Abu-Alhassan of the Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities.
This extraordinary site has a 30 year plan and is currently 15 percent through it within 3 years. The conference ended on Thursday evening with a dinner and a theatrical performance.
The agenda for the conference was to make connections with conservation and restoration groups and to showcase the projects of APSAD. Certainly this was achieved and with the aim of trying to secure funding for APSAD, hopefully some of these connections will come into fruition. The next stage is to maintain these contacts and to try and develop the relationships to a point where APSAD will receive more support.

...واذا لم يرمم فان مصيره الزوال .

**********

نحن المجتكع الرافض للحروب ....

....مجتمع الثقافة والجمال ....

نحن مجتمع ، طائفتنا الحضارة .

ان الفوضى الفكرية المنتشرة حولنا ، هي اداة ضعف لن نقبل بها ....

لن نقبل ان يكون الضعف ساكنا فينا .. فلنعمل على ائتلاف ضمائر تتميز بالشجاعة زالثابرة ، لنبني مستقبلا لأجيالنا ، ونرمم سويا الفكر والحجر من أطلال ماضينا .

***********

ان جمعية " الأبساد " وبلدية بعبدا بشخص رئيسها واعضائها مستعدتان كل الأستعداد لتقومان بما يلزم وبأي مجهود من اجل اعادة العز والمكانة الى هذا الصرح العريق .

امسيتنا اليوم موسيقى وفرح ، فلنستمع الى باقة مميزة من فناني بلادنا يهمسون في اذاننا انشودة للجمال والبقاء . وشكرا

title: National Heritage Day
summary: On the occasion of the National Heritage Day 2013, APSAD organized in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture, guided visits to 10 regions of Lebanon on 15, 16 and 17 may 2013 including :Kamid el-Loz, Machghara, Kherbet Kanafar, Aamiq…
content:
On the occasion of the National Heritage Day 2013, APSAD organized in cooperation with the Ministry of Culture, guided visits to 10 regions of Lebanon on 15, 16 and 17 may 2013 including :

Kamid el-Loz, Machghara, Kherbet Kanafar, Aamiq, Sarafand, Aadloun, Maghdoucheh, Achmoun, Deir el Ahmar, Bechwat and Barqa.

Voluntary guides appointed by the municipalities of each region accompanied the visitors . Each visit was attended by more than 50 participants.

Visit to Kamid el-Loz, Machghara, Kherbet Kanafar, Aamiq : on 15/5/2013

►Kamid el-Loz : We have been received by the municipality of the village. After exchanging of welcome and a brief information about the village, a breakfast was offered to the visitors.

Before leaving the municipality , we offered the mayor 2 books published by APSAD.
We visited the Bronze Age archeological sites and the prehistoric caves of the village.

►Machghara : We visited the village, some water springs, ancient leather workshops, and the house of Lebanese musician and compositor Zaki Nassif , recently donated to APSAD.

►Aammiq : We headed out to the beautiful wetlands reserve in Aammiq, an area significant for breeding and migrating birds and one of the very few wetlands left in Lebanon. We saw water surfaces, reed beds, and endless surrounding fields and meadows in this bird watching area, located along a major migration route from Asia to Africa.

►Kherbet Kanafar : The Schneller School
The Johann Ludwig Schneller Orphanage School was founded in 1952 in Kherbet Kanafar where Christian and Muslim children and adolescents grow up side by side. This place looks like a GREEN paradise and all is CLEAN…

Visit to Sarafand, Aadloun, Maghdoucheh, Achmoun on 16/5/2013:

►Sarafand :
Sarafand is renowned for its manufacture of blown glass. Beautiful multicoloured vases and glasses were glittering on the shelves . Ali Khalifeh, one of the last manufacturers, explained to the visitors the process of blown glass.
We also visited Sarepta, where an ancient phenician port is located.

►Aadloun :
We were received by the municipality of the village and its mayor Samih Wehbé. We offered them 2 books published by APSAD. Around the village we visited the archeological
sites, many prehistoric caves and the Maqam Nabi Sari. The lunch was served on the sea side, with fish mezze and salads.

►Maghdoucheh :
The visitors were given a precious moment of rest and self concentration at Notre Dame of Maghdoucheh.

►On our way to Saïda we visited Echmoun’s archeological site and Temple dating of the VIIe – Vie century bef.. J.-C.
Visit to Deir el Ahmar, Bechwat and Barqa on 17/5/2013:

►Deir el Ahmar :
We were invited by WADA " Women’s Association of Deir el Ahmar " an organization for Rural Eco-tourism and Agri-tourism in the region of Deir El Ahmar founded by Mrs Dunia Khoury. Mrs Khoury showed a slide presentation of her association’s objectives and activities . This organization has won in 2002 the “Dubai International Award for Best Practices to improve the living environment ”.

The breakfast was prepared by WADA’s women.

Our visit also included one of the eight historic churches of Deir el Ahmar.

►Bechwat :
The visitors prayed at the Mar Saba Monastery.

►Barqa :

►The mokhtar of the village Mr Sami Geagea, welcomed us. We offered him 2 books published by APSAD.

►We visited Dany Geagea’s biological farm of and its dairy products. He currently has several cows and 10 ostriches.

We were invited for a wine tasting at the local winery owned by the Geagea family.

►We visited a health Center run by the Sœurs des Saints Cœurs where 8 doctors in turn take care of the health of nearby villagers, and a sewing workshop where 40 women work to improve their living.

►Above the village we saw the biggest reserve of Juniper trees, Mamlaket el Lezzab .

Our visit ended with a good lunch at the mokhtar’s residence, an eagle’s nest at the top of the mountains.

This was our Heritage Day visits for the year 2013, an unforgettable one. All the participants were enthusiastic and delighted to have discovered little-known areas of Lebanon.

content:
On September 21st, 2012, around three hundred fifty persons among whom ministers, deputies, ambassadors, businessmen, members of APSAD and festivals’ organisors, gathered in the hall of the Baabda Sérail , one of the oldest public building built around 1775 , to attend a concert organized by APSAD. The event took place under the patronage of H.E. Mr Gaby Layoun, Minister of Culture and with the collaboration of the Polish embassy in Lebanon.

The program included soprano Nadine Nassar, harpe Anna Sikorzak-Olek, and the Quintette à cordes de Beyrouth directed by Robert Kfouri.

Mrs Raya Daouk, APSAD President, opened the ceremony with the following impressive speech- in french:

 “Notre patrimoine est la dette dont les créanciers sont nos enfants.

Il est de notre devoir de préserver notre mémoire, notre culture, notre identité, et tirer la sonnette d'alarme pour trier nos souvenirs et valoriser ces beaux sites mus par une irrésistible volonté de tendre vers la plénitude de leur éclat.

Dans un pays en proie aux convulsions et aux violences aveugles, nous voyons bien que la beauté persiste.

A travers elle, nous acquérons le sens du divin, de la perfection.
Nous gardons une capacité étonnante à recoudre le tissu social maintes fois déchiré.

Nous n'oublions guère nos drames, seulement nous les intégrons dans notre œuvre dans des temps différents.

Participer à la création, restaurer, pour se forger une irréductible identité est une aspiration à la pérennité de notre existence.

Notre pays, si ravissant par la force des contrastes, la violence des inquiétudes et la douceur de l'art de vivre, mutilé par des guerres , n'est pas fait pour mourir mais pour inventer la vie.

Quoique déchue de son ancienne splendeur, cette terre de feu, avec un peu de discipline intellectuelle, pourrait redevenir un écrin à nos talents ainsi qu'à nos monuments, pour valider nos souvenirs.

Notre gout pour la vie , avec la BEAUTÉ pour RELIGION , sauverait notre patrimoine.

Voyez ce splendide monument chargé d'histoire, qui va chanter ce soir un hymne à la vie avec une superbe mosaïque d’artistes, nous émeut par sa beauté..

Comme la belle architecture, la musique, selon Confucius, est un enseignement sans paroles. Il s'adresse directement à l'âme, et par la dynamique du geste qui les fait naître, exprime notre être intime.

Ce soir, nous célébrons la musique avec nos artistes venus de loin pour nous donner ces bons moments.

Nous célébrons aussi la noblesse de l'architecture, art si bien maîtrisé par un des grands de ce pays , Monsieur ASSEM SALAM qui a consacré sa vie à son art, à ses croyances profondes, son culte du beau et du pur; sans compromis, sans tricher avec lui-même.

Tel un monument, il s’est élevé à des cimes pour faire un lien de beauté entre terre et ciel et sublimer son art.

En musique, ce soir, nous célébrons son art, et l'APSAD qu'il a porté dans son cœur et intégré dans sa vie, lui remet un gage d'honneur et d'affection en guise de fidélité à sa personnalité hors du commun!

Merci. »

With her crystal voice Nadine Nassar appeared to the public with arias from Claude Debussy, Frédéric Chopin, Enrico Toselli, Haendel Hahn, Puccini, and was greeted with applause.

Anna Sikorzak-Olek the magic harpist and the Quintette à cordes de Beyrouth, five musicians, gave to this memorable evening its unforgettable touch.

A cocktail was served to the public at the end of the program.

APSAD was proud to present such a valuable program to the public.

content:
National Heritage day 2012

APSAD organized National Heritage day 2012 with the collaboration of the ministry of Culture on 23/5/2012 in Hermel and on 24/5/2012 in Tyre. The objective of this event was to increase public awareness for the preservation of the heritage.

Hermel : Solar power lights illuminate highway to Hermel. The lights are meant to both increase road safety and to preserve the environment.

Visited places in Hermel:

> Mar Maroun Monastry: which is a rock-cut structure in three levels. It is said to be the temporary refuge of the successors of Saint Maroun, founder of the Maronite Christian sect in the fourth century.

> Qasr el Banât : ancient site

> The spring of the Orontes (Assi) River called Ain El Zarka spring :
Assi river (450km) is fed by many streams coming from the mountains of northern Lebanon.

> Pyramid of El Qamouat of Hermel:
On a hill-top stands a stone tower capped by a pyramid known as the Pyramid of El Qamouat. This historic monument dates back to the second century before Christ. It points upward like a finger and stands like a lighthouse.

> Dardara Cascades :
Located in Dardara, Hermel, Lebanon. Offers hotel rooms and suites, restaurants and sports activities.

>The city

>The municipality: On this occasion the municipality of Hermel gave us a motorized guide who accompanied us everywhere during our visit to Hermel. The president and some members of the municipality received us warmly with a traditional tea. APSAD offered their library two books “l’Habitation au Liban” and “Connaissance du Liban”

> Fekha ou Fiké :
Is a village in northeastern Lebanon , north of the Bekaa valley , residents are called Fikanis . Once famous for its carpets.

Tyr: The history of Tyr merges with the history of Sidon mainly due to the fact that, over
several periods, the two cities were unified. It attracted great conquerors such as the Babylonian King Nabuchodonosor and Alexander the Great. The merchants of Tyr were the first who ventured to navigate the Mediterranean waters.

Visited places in Tyr:

> The ruins of Tyr: Recent excavations have uncovered Crusader, Arab, Byzantine and Greco-Roman remains.
> Phoenician walls
> Main avenue lined with a colonnade and sidewalk
> The Great Hippodrome for chariot racing a remarkable stone built structure
> The old district
> Grid-like streets,
>Two churches “Notre Dame de la mer” and “ Saint Thomas”
> Necropolis (city of the dead)
> The Triumphal Arch: that is composed of a Necropolis situated on both sides of a long avenue is the most impressive of its remains.
>The harbor and the fishermen

Qana :

>The city that witnessed a miracle of Jesus Christ first when he turned water into wine at the wedding in Qana.

> Near Qana Statues and sculptures in stone which give the evidence to the miracle.

Ras el Aïn :
Is one of the villages of Tyre in the South Province where there are three springs of fresh water.

title: APSAD's Jubilee
summary: A fabulous concert took place on the evening of Friday, May 18, 2012 at the Grand Serail on the occasion of APSAD’s jubilee under the patronage of the Prime Minister HE Mr. Nagib Mikati with the collaboration of HE Mr.Gaby Layoun Minister…
content:
A fabulous concert took place on the evening of Friday, May 18, 2012 at the Grand Serail on the occasion of APSAD’s jubilee under the patronage of the Prime Minister HE Mr. Nagib Mikati with
the collaboration of HE Mr.Gaby Layoun Minister of Culture.

This event was sponsored by ALFA, Byblos Bank and UFA Insurance.

300 guests were present including HE Mr. Walid Daouk Minister of Information,
Mr. Joseph Abdelahad representing HE Mr. Charbel Nahas Minister of Labour,
Mr. Michel de Chadarevian representing HE Mr. Gaby Layoun Minister of Culture,
Mrs Gaby Layoun, HE Mr. Hassan Diab Minister of Education,HE Mr. Alain Tabourian,
HE Mr. Nicolas Sehnaoui Minister of Telecommunications,President Adnan Kassar,
HE Mr. Maurice Sehnaoui, HE Mrs Leyla Solh Hamadé President of Al Walid Bin Talal
Humanitarian Foundation, HE Mr Farid Raphaël, HE Mr. Ibrahim Najjar, Mrs May Arida
Honorary President of Baalbeck International Festival, Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane
Founder and Honorary President of APSAD, Mr. Amine Daouk President of Makassed ,
all the sponsors and their guests and a big number of members and friends of the
assocation.

LBCI made the coverage of the event.

Just after the Lebanese Anthem, Mrs Raya Daouk, APSAD President, delivered her speech.
She was applauded wholeheartedly.

The 95 musicians of the Lebanese Philharmonic Orchestra conducted by Maestro Harout Fazlian interpreted Ludwig van Beethoven’s 5th symphony : Allegro con brio, Andante con moto, Allegro, Allegro, followed by Naji Hakim’s Ouverture Libanaise, Franz Liszt’s Hungarian Rhapsody no.2, Jacques Offenbach’s Barcarolle from the “Tales of Hoffman” and ended with Giuseppe Verdi’s Grand March from “Aïda” which was applauded on foot.

The concert was just a big success.

Three persons were honored during this event.

> Mrs. Gaby Layoun decorated Lady Yvonne Sursock as Knight of the National Order of the Cedar for her 90th anniversary and also as one of the APSAD’s Founder for her fierce fighting and forbidding the destruction of old buildings in Lebanon through APSAD for 50 years, and
Mrs Raya Daouk and the committee gave her an APSAD trophy.

> HE Mrs. Layla Solh Hamadé was honored by an APSAD trophy given by Mrs Raya Daouk for
her generous donation to APSAD projects.

> Mrs Raya Daouk, APSAD President, was honored by a trophy given by Mrs Gaby Layoun for her endless effort to keep APSAD on foot in its coming projects.

The cocktail offered to the guests after the concert included a birthday cake celebrating the 90th birthday of Lady Yvonne Cochrane who cut it surrounded by all her family and friends accompanied by a violinist, followed by another birthday cake celebrating Apsad Jubilee that was cut by Mrs Raya Daouk, Lady Yvonne Cochrane and HE Mrs Leila Solh Hamadé.

content:
Our friends and members once again attended a fabulous concert on the occasion of APSAD’s 50th jubilee under the patronage of HE the Minister of Culture Gaby Layoun on Saturday, October 8, 2011 in the hall of the National Museum.

There was an important number of Beirut’s diplomatic personalities such as:
HE the Minister of Culture Mr Gaby Layoun, MP Dr. Nagi Gharios, HE the Minister of Justice Mr Chakib Qortbawi, HE the Minister of Telecommunications Mr Nicolas Sehnaoui, HE the Ambassador
of Romania Mr Daniel Tanase, HE the Ambassador of Egypt Mr Mohamad Taoufic, Mrs Nadia Aoun, Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane, Honorary President of APSAD and a good number of journalists………

The concert titled ‹The Song of the immortals› was performed by:
Ms Samar Salameh, soprano, Mrs Olga Bolun, piano, the ‹The Musique d’Harmonie› of the Lebanese army directed by Colonel Herro and the choral of the Antonine university directed by Father Toufic Maatouk.

The programme consisted of selected extracts from Verdi, Bellini, Handel, Gluck, Kurt Weil, Bizet, Fairouz.

The audience enjoyed the dazzling performance of Ms Samar Salameh , as well as all the other members of the choral and Colonel Herro directing the orchestra. It was a refined programme.

On this occasion the President of APSAD Mrs Raya Daouk pronounced the following speech :

جعمية (APSAD) تشكر الحضور الكريم

تشكر حاكمية مصرف لبنان لمساعدتنا في انجاز هذا اللقاء . وخصوصا تشكر وزارة الثقافة بشخص معالي الوزير غابي ليون وبمساعدة السيدة عفيش المسؤولة عن المتحف لاعطائنا الفرصة بأن تفتح ابواب هذا الصرح العريق كي نتذكر ولا نعيد تجربة الويلات التي حلت بالوطن وخاصة في هذا الموقع بالذات وهو رمز لكل معاناتنا في حقبة سوداء من تاريخنا حين كانت تتساقط الحجارة وتنفجر القنابل ، فعدونا يأسا واغترابا ... ثم رجعنا !

ان الحياة والموت لصيقان ، والحياة اقوى ، تتغلب على الموت ، تنبعث منه وتحييه ... في الذاكرة وفي الأفعال ، وايضا في الفن وكل انجازات المرء ...فيكون هذا تراثنا للغد.

ان حاضر المرء مرأة للذاكرة ، ولا حياة له الا بالذاكرة وهي تستثير الفكر الذي يولد الابداع ... والابداع يعلي شأن الانسان ويخلده ويعلمه من تجارب الحياة .

العلم بفسر سلوك الانسان ، والثقافة توجهه!

امسيتنا اليوم حلقة من مسلسل الأمسيات التي نقدمها لاحياء ذكرى اليوبيل الذهبي لجمعية ( ال(APSAD هي تجربة فنية تداعب الحجر ، عله يتكلم عن اجدادنا.

يكاد يقول اننا اناسا جمعتنا جغرافية واحدة وثقافة واحدة حول حوض بحر معطاء .

مهدالأديان والحضارات المختلفة التي أغنت شعوب المنطقة واصبح تراثنا متشابه ومتداخل .

لو، سمعنا همسات حجارة التاريخ هذه لقالت لنا : دعوا الخلافات جانبا وتوحدوا حول تاريخكم وثقافتكم .

أحلامنا كبيرة . انجازاتنا صغيرة . لكنها ، هي ، زوادتنا في ضرورة العيش ..ثم يخلق الابداع ... من رحم الأوهام والأمال .

لنستمع اليوم ما تقول لنا هذه التحف الدفينة الساكنة حين تستفيق معنا ... في هذا المكان الرائع !

ريا الداعوق

title: National Heritage Day 2011
summary: National heritage day - may 2011On the occasion of the national heritage day and with the collaboration of the ministry of Culture, APSAD organized on may 18,20,26, 2011 guided visits to Rachaya-Anjar, Akkar, Zahlé, each one attended by…
content:
National heritage day - may 2011

On the occasion of the national heritage day and with the collaboration of the ministry of Culture, APSAD organized on may 18,20,26, 2011 guided visits to Rachaya-Anjar, Akkar, Zahlé, each one attended by more than 70 visitors.

On May 18, 2011 visit to Rachaya and Anjar.
  • We admired the all green Rashaya al-Wadi located on the slopes of Mount Hermon in Lebanon , the terraced gardens, thousand red-brick houses and its main street known as the “souq” leading up to the citadel.
  • The historic "Castle of independence"
  • The municipality
  • Two old churches

Buildings back to the year 1370.

At noon the visitors had lunch in Anjar.

Anjar is a town located in the Bekaa valley it is the unique site of Lebanon of the era of the omeyyades.

Among the monuments we visited:

  • Anjar’s citadel dated from 18thth century
  • Armenian orthodoxe church St. Paul and some historical monuments
  • The spring

On May 20, 2011 a guided visit to Akkar.

On our way we visited:

  • Tell Arqa a famous archeological site near the village of Minyara where the roman emperor Sèvère Alexandre was born in 208.
  • Kobayat: The museum of butterflies and birds; The Carmelite church.
  • Touring the old town of Akkar.
  • Beyno the residence of HE Mr. Issam Fares where lunch was offered to the visitors.
  • Private natural reserve of HE and the artificial lake.
  • Borj and its serail . The serail partly restored has a historical value . We saw an old olive oil press, the old stables, the gibbet which served to apply justice judgment.

On may 26, 2011 visit to Zahle.

In Zahle, we were received by Mr. Issam Kharrat, representing the association of APSAD in Zahleh, and his son Fady. After welcoming the visitors he left leaving Fady with us for visiting the old houses.

In Zahle we visited :

  • The archbishop residence of greek catholics and the monastery of St Eli of Toa.
  • The old houses of Hindi and Jeha where flowers all around the houses welcome you. We had a look at the rooms; the beds, wardrobes, the curtains the frames of photos all details were from around 1930. So much love and respect for the memory of their past.
  • The municipality of Zahlé where we were received by the president of the municipality Mr. Joseph Diab Maalouf and his team. After welcoming us, the president made a short speech in which he mentioned that in Zahle there were around one thousand old houses which are mostly restored by their owners. He said that the protection of the old houses must continue to encourage tourism.

Time was running. The president and his team invited all the visitors to Alberto hotel for lunch. The lebanese cuisine was excellent.

Around 4 o’clock we thanked the president and his team for their special attention to the visitors.

On our way to Beirut we visited:

  • Ksara. Rania Chammas, public relation of the domain along with her explanation about the vine and the caves presented a documentary film of the growth of grapes to the preparation of vine.

This was the end of our third guided visit to Zahle.

title: Heritage Day Kesrwan/Jbeil
summary: On the occasion of the National Heritage Day, APSAD Kesrouan/Jbeil organized guided visits in the caza of Jbeil. Those visits included:>Maad village and the church of the Saint Charbel where we admired Byzantine paintings dated from XIIth…
content:
On the occasion of the National Heritage Day, APSAD Kesrouan/Jbeil organized guided visits in the caza of Jbeil.

Those visits included:

>Maad village and the church of the Saint Charbel where we admired Byzantine paintings dated from XIIth century, hand made crafts’ exhibition and ready cooked dishes prepared by the countrywomen.

>Mayfouk village where we visited Notre Dame d’Elige the maronite patriarchal headquarter during two centuries from 1120 to 1440 and the convent where stands the historic icon of St. Virgin Mary at an altitude of 1100m.

>Behdidat village where we visited an old maronite church called Saint Théodore where we admired beautiful wall paintings representing personalities of the Old and New Testament.

There were around fifty visitors for this visit which was accompanied by an experienced guide from the National Museum.

Lunch was offered to the visitors at Mayfouk’s convent.

On the other hand the Kesrouan/Jbeil organized a lunch at the Odyssée restaurant in Hotel
Byblos-Sur-Mer to celebrate its 10 years activities and also to honor Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane the Founder and Honorary President of APSAD.

On this occasion Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane delivered the following speech in french.

“Malgré les déclarations du gouvernement, relatifs à la protection du patrimoine le pays se
dégrade journellement.

Le Liban est devenu semblable à un fruit que l’on mange et dont on jette les épluchures.

Nous avons une démocratie avec d’excellents ministres mais hélas un parlement, sauf quelques exceptions composé d’ignares sans culture, pour qui l’argent seul compte et nous avons des entrepreneurs également sans culture dont le rêve est de copier Dubaï.

C’est dans ce marasme que se débat lAPSAD, et le comité Beyrouth – Kesrouan est heureusement demeuré très actif et c’est grâce à lui que quelques beaux bâtiments ont pu échapper au massacre environnant.

Puisse son exemple se repercuter ailleurs au Liban.”

Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane
Fondatrice et Présidente Honoraire de l’APSAD

title: Concert
summary: On the 2d and 3d of may APSAD celebrated it’s glorious fiftieth anniversary. All members and friends were invited to participate to this memorable evening of music. Francesca Micarelli, Soprano, accompanied by the pianist Maestro Massimo…
content:
On the 2d and 3d of may APSAD celebrated it’s glorious fiftieth anniversary.
All members and friends were invited to participate to this memorable evening of music.

Francesca Micarelli, Soprano, accompanied by the pianist Maestro Massimo Lambertini, who came especially for this occasion from Italy, interpreted excerpts from Rossini, Liszt, Donizetti, Shuman, Schubert, Wagner-Liszt, Gounod, Mascagni.

Among the presents were seen: the minister of Culture Mr. Selim Wardy, the minister of Justice Mr. Ibrahim Najjar, Lama and Tammam Salam, Nadia Michel Aoun, Laure Doumit, Nayla et Semaan Bassil, Paula and Nicolas Sehnaoui, the ambassadors of Germany, Italy and Mexico….

Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane, Honorary president of APSAD and Mrs. Raya Daouk actual president of APSAD, addressed the following speeches in french, on this occasion.

Here are the speeches of both presidents :

Au Liban, plus ça change et plus c’est la même chose. Hélas hélas ! Je dirai même que plus ça change et plus nous reculons vers l’abîme de l’ignorance et des fausses valeurs. Il est évident que dans ce marasme auquel on doit ajouter la cupidité, le Liban agonise, il agonise derrière le paravent d’une pléthore de voitures rutilantes, de restaurants flamboyants où se meurt même le souvenir de l’une des cuisines les plus délicieuses et variées, témoin de vieille civilisation. Il en va de même pour notre architecture telle qu’elle était, l’une des plus ravissantes, élégantes et raffinées du bassin méditerranéen.

La copie et surtout la mauvaise copie de Manhattan et maintenant de Dubaï est devenue le
«Trade mark » de nos villes.

Quant à nos villages, autrefois parmi les plus charmants que l’on puisse imaginer, disparus comme par l’effet de la fée carabosse et remplacés par un magma de béton informe et peut être pire encore par un placage de pierres appliqué sur des structures innommables.

Y a t-il espoir de remédier à ce lamentable état des choses ! Pour ceux qui sont conscients du désastre il n’y a qu’un espoir: la mise sur pied d’une municipalité; non pas la mascarade en pièces détachées que nous osons appeler municipalité mais une véritable structure cohérente où des équipes d’architectes, d’urbanistes, d’avocats et de médecins interviennent sur les décisions à prendre. Les permis de construire ou de détruire ne seraient donc plus obtenus par des enveloppes offertes à tel ou tel individu.

L’APSAD s’est donc engagée dans cette voie avec l’aide d’un groupe de jeunes et d’étudiants conscients de l’épouvantable avenir urbain qui les attend.

Notre espoir est que les moins jeunes se réveillent et participent à la lutte, pas nécessairement par des « sit in » ou des manifestations qui sont du ressort des jeunes, mais en se joignant aux efforts de l’APSAD auprès des dirigeants de ce pays et surtout au niveau des députés. Dieu fasse qu’un jour , pas trop lointain, nous puissions éliminer ce cauchemar et nous réveiller sur des paysages urbains ayant retrouvé cohérence et dignité ainsi que sur une montagne revenue
à sa beauté première.

Yvonne Sursock Cochrane
Honorary President

Ce soir commencent les célébrations de l’année cinquantenaire de l’APSAD , première association pour la protection du patrimoine et de l’environnement fondée par Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane, Assem Salam, Camille Aboussouan et plusieurs grandes figures libanaises.

C’était la première association fondée dans ce domaine au Liban et dans le monde arabe.

Nous n’allons pas parler de certaines de nos réussites, mais plutôt de là où nous avons échoué, car uniquement avec votre aide nous pourrions poursuivre notre pénible route à travers un pays souvent meurtri par les guerres.

Là où nous avons échoué c’est l’instauration d’une loi sur la protection de nos sites et demeures. Il est imperative de se mobiliser pour arriver à sauver ce précieux patrimoine qui nous reste encore.

Sauver ne signifie pas seulement intervenir dans la destinée d’une œuvre, en vue de s’assurer qu’elle va éclore et refleurir , il faut faire vivre l’œuvre qu’elle porte en elle car c’est là où réside leur immortalité.

Ce soir, dans ce lieu magnifique où Dieu nous émeut, nos yeux ont la vue courte quand ils regardent l’immortalité d’une œuvre dans son infinie beauté.

Pour honorer ce lieu sublime joyau d’une civilization liée à nos racines , écrin d’une famille dont le combat sans faiblesse est mené à travers des vies entières, nous vivrons un hymne à la beauté à la musique et surtout à la vie après la vie !

Nous vous remercions de votre présence et de l’aide que chaque personne a apporté pour que ces moments uniques restent gravés dans nos mémoires.

Raya Daouk
APSAD President

A cocktail was offered to the guests during the intermission.

Our sponsor for this concert was Byblos Bank

content:
In the framework of APSAD musical walks on may 29,2010, the members of the executive committee invited their friends and supporters to the 4th annual concert featuring soprano Maria Christina Fakhoury, baritone Teddy Nasr and pianist Olga Bolun in the Dagher’s family palace in Gemayzeh. FN 13 Group sponsored the concert. The young and talented artists who interpreted excerpts from Schuman, Puccini, Lehar, and Mozart were greatly applauded by the audience.

Mrs. Raya Daouk, president of APSAD, said in her speech:

"Our capital Beirut is being destroyed, is it normal that whatever remains of it is the result of the raging cries of offended citizens having suffered a huge destructive wave that was smashing our heritage? The old souks disappeared, what is left are bits and pieces to be protected.

Our past is the heart of our present… and our memories dwell in these splendid houses, witnesses of a golden age, as well as of injuries and dramas due to the war. If we want to relate our present it is essential to consider that our past is the basis of it and our memories are such
as steam evaporating from our hard work, that takes us towards the noblest. Evil dissolves in the darkness of memory, nothing stays except examples and lessons, let us work and fight in order to safeguard our heritage so that we could leave to future generations the murmur of a disappeared civilization; for who leaves no imprints disappears without return.

This evening is an evening of songs and joy in this beautiful palace, a palace preserved by many generations of a big Lebanese family who lived in it, took care of it with warmth and nobility… If life gives us wealth let us enjoy it, for who loves life, protects his past, and who flirts with destruction marries death.

Let us greet today the hymn to beauty and our presence in this old
palace so that our joy tonight be at the same time ammunitions and exhilaration for the sake of our continuity."

Raya Daouk
APSAD President

content:
S.Arabia - June 2010

H.E. Mr Fadi Abboud , Lebanese minister of Tourism invited Apsad to participate at the First International Conference for Urban Heritage in the Islamic Countries in Riyadh, from the 22d to the 25th of May 2010.

APSAD represented there by architect Hana Alamuddine Haydar ex member of APSAD executive committee with the help of Ghassan Yazbek set up in our own stand a full exhibition of 13 panels showing the various aspects of our built heritage and prepared a 15 minute projection of the built heritage in Salimah (Metn).

The exhibition was very successful. H.R.H. Prince Sultan Bin Salman who was very impressed with our stand promised to visit in the near future our offices in Beirut. We were honored to offer him a copy of the book " Palaces of Lebanon".

The exhibition was well received, as it was a unique experience of a public collaboration with a private realm that concerns the protection of our heritage.

REPORT OF ARCHITECT HANA ALAMUDDINE HAYDAR FOR THE ABOVE CONFERENCE

As you are aware, Apsad, was asked to pariticipate in the First International Conference for Urban Heritage in the Islamic Countries in Riyadh by our Minister of Tourism.

Apsad, sent and mounted a full exibition of 13 panels showing the various aspects of our built heritage and prepared a 15 minute presentation on the protection of the built heritage of Salimah.
The exhibition was very succesful. His Royal Highness Prince Sultan Bin Salman was very impressed with the exhibition and promised to visit our offices in Beirut . We also presented him with a copy of the book " Palaces of Lebanon".

The presentation was well received as it was a unique experience of collaboration of the public and private realm for the protection of heritage.

A word of thanks to Ghassan Yazbek who went ahead of me and mounted the exhibition beautifully.

Finallly on behalf of Apsad, I would like to thank our Minister of Tourism Mr. Fadi Abboud who gave us this opportunity to take part in this very interesting and valuable conference.

Best regards
Hana Alamuddin Haidar

content:
On the occasion of the national heritage day and with the collaboration of the ministry of Culture, APSAD organized on may 20,21,22, 2010 guided visits to the most famous Lebanese writer’s houses in Beit Chabab / Fraykeh / Besharreh /Ehden / Baskinta / Choukhroub / each one attended by more than 50 visitors.

On May 20, 2010 a guided visit to Beit Chabab and Fraykeh.

• Beit Chabab the handicraft traditional weaving
• Renowned bells workshop
• Pottery workshop.
• Mrs. Yolla Hadifé’s domain: 4 old beautiful houses recently renovated in a genuine style.
Mrs. Dolly Khawam member of the executive committee gave Mrs. Hadifeh Apsad’s honorary gift in gratitude to her warm hospitality.
• Fraykeh: Amine El Rihani museum.
Dr. Rihani, the writer’s grand nephew, commented to the visitors some family’s photos, the author’s book published in Arabic and English, his notebooks and other personal things, his office, his typewriter.. Mrs. Dolly Khawam gave Dr. Rihani in gratitude to his availability, Apsad’s honorary gift that has been displayed among other important objects in the Museum.

On May 21, 2010 Bsharreh and Ehden Horsh.

•Besharreh: A guided visit to Gebran Khalil Gebran Museum. Booklets were distributed to follow his historical and biographical productions displayed in every showroom. A selection of furniture belonging to the artist proof of the simple but pleasant lifestyle.

• Ehden / The Horch (forest)
This reserve is classified. There are 2,863 species of plants, 212 of them are considered rare, 126 species on the way of disappearance, 78 species of medicinal plants.

On May 22, 2010 in Baskinta and Choukhroub.

• Baskinta
Mrs. Zakieh Naimi Bassil, actual director of Eastwood college, the writer’s, Mikhael Naime, grand-niece, received the visitors in the writer’s room ,and told them about his life, his mystical way of thinking and writing and his works.

• Choukhroub: A visit to the writer’s tomb and statue.
A visit to the cave on a nearby hill where Mikael Naime meditated and wrote.

• At the end of the day the visitors stopped at the foot of Sannine mountain to drink fresh water from a generous water spring.

title: Concert
summary: In the framework of its musical walks, APSAD (Association for the Protection of Sites and Old Residences in Lebanon) organized a concert on the 12th of October 2009, at Sursock Palace, residence of Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane, with the…
content:
In the framework of its musical walks, APSAD (Association for the Protection of Sites and Old Residences in Lebanon) organized a concert on the 12th of October 2009, at Sursock Palace, residence of Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane, with the participation of :

• Spinto soprano Maria Christina Fakhoury
• Baritone Fernando Afara

This concert was organized for the benefit of the association.

On this occasion Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane APSAD founder and Honorary president delivered the following speech in French.

Chers amis ici présents,

Je vous répète ce soir les prières adressées en 2000 à l’occasion du concert de l’Orchestre Philarmonique de chambre de Rome avec l’apport du grand violoniste Uto Ughi.

Les mêmes exhortations furent adressées le 12 avril 2003.

Croyez-moi, si vous ne faites pas l’effort de vous joindre à ceux qui ont à cœur les destinées de ce pays, en l’occurrence l’APSAD, rien qu’en donnant la minime somme réclamée pour être membre ou encore mieux en prenant une part active dans ses activités. Il ne restera plus un coin de ce pays autrefois si beau à léguer à vos enfants. Gardez présent à votre mémoire ces quelques lignes de Lamartine car elles sont un témoignage venu de l’extérieur, de ce que fut le Liban :

[…Quand les sentiers devenaient trop rapides, nous laissions nos montures un moment, et nous parcourions à pied les terrasses naturelles ou artificielles qui forment des gradins de verdure de toute la colline de San-Dimitri. Dans mon enfance, je me suis représenté souvent ce paradis terrestre, cet Eden que toutes les nations ont dans leurs souvenirs, soit comme un beau rêve, soit comme une tradition d’un temps et d’un séjour plus parfaits; j’ai suivi Milton dans ses délicieuses déscriptions de ce séjour enchanté de nos premiers parents; mais ici, comme en toutes choses, la nature surpasse infiniment l’imagination. Dieu n’a pas donné à l’homme de rêver aussi beau qu’il l’a fait. J’avais rêvé Eden, je puis dire que je l’ai vu..]
Lamartine

Et également j’ajouterai trois textes d’Ernest Renan, de Gustave Flaubert et l’autre de Jérôme et Jean Tharaud :

Tout ce que je puis vous dire, c’est que l’air
Du Liban est le plus suave, le plus pur , le plus
Vivifiant du monde, que ce pays inspire la gaîté,
Le repos, la tranquillité d’esprit, une activité
Bienfaisante et tempérée…
Ernest Renan

J’ai la mer sous mes fenêtres, un peu plus loin
Beyrouth entouré de mûriers et à ma droite le
Liban qui a une cravate de nuages et une
Perruque de neige
Gustave Flaubert

Et devant…ces villages en plein ciel
Comme des nids de pies, ces gracieuses
Maisons en arcades,…on songe invinciblement
A ces extraordinaires bibelots, à
Ces étonnants tours de force, que réalise
Avec amour, pendant des années et des
Années, quelque artisan passionné.
Jérome et Jean Tharaud

Est-ce bien le Liban que ces lignes décrivent, l’on a peine à le croire.

Joignez-vous donc à l’APSAD et à d’autres organisations dont les buts sont complémentaires de façon à promouvoir une fédération d’associations dont
le pouvoir serait déterminant auprès des autorités.

Hélas, l’apathie, l’ignorance, l’absence de lois et un tas d’autres facteurs ont réduit le Liban à ce qu’il est aujourd’hui. Cependant, un effort collectif de vous tous ici présents, permettrait de préserver une certaine mémoire, quelques paysages, quelques trésors d’architecture afin que nous ne donnions pas l’impression d’être unpeuple sans passé et aussi afin que les jeunes générations aient un point d’appui, les racines nécessaires à la création d’une nouvelle architecture qui ne soit pas batarde.

En ce qui concerne la cravate de neige au Sannine qui est le réservoir d’eau du Liban, je me permets de vous informer que l’APSAD a réussi à stopper, j’espère définitivement, un projet de développement touristique sur la crête qui aurait bloqué le drainage des eaux provenant de la fonte des neiges vers les sources de ce pays. Le Liban aurait alors l’aspect d’un désert.

Ne décevez donc pas les générations à venir ; c’est vous qu’ils blâmeront lorsque le Liban sera réduit à n’être plus qu’un bidonville généralisé.

Lady Yvonne Sursock Cochrane
Fondatrice et Présidente Honoraire de l’APSAD

The concert was sponsored by FRANSABANK

content:
In the framework of its musical walks, APSAD has organized its second concert on December 21 2009 inside the premises of the splendid Moawad Museum.

Around one hundred friends of APSAD enjoyed listening once again to Spinto Soprano Christina Fakhoury and Baritone Fernando Afara singing their beautiful Christmas arias and carols.

On this occasion President Raya Daouk delivered the following speech:

“Our real homeland is this state that is beyond time: our heritage.
It has no dimension in time or space.
Our soul’s hidden path happens to be in our history; and it is the meaning of our life.

Without our history, we forsake all our references, all the landmarks on which lean our senses and our reason.

The progress made by science and technology has never been able to find the chemical existence of the soul. It is just the history of humanity and its knowledge that makes it come alive again; that is why we should always ask and discover if we want to grow, and above all we must know how to preserve our history and our civilization to better prepare our future.
In spite of all the daily difficulties we face to preserve what history has bequeathed, in spite of the world struggles against the spoiling interests of a certain savage capitalism that falls on us, some people with much sacrifice have been able to preserve some haven of beauty and happiness in our country as certain places that we have the pleasure to discover with these musical walks organized by APSAD.

It is a sudden awareness of what has been done to try to stop the collective massacre of our memory on the sanctuary of the anarchistic construction.

We will need all our efforts; people like you and me who are doing some sacrifices to arouse in us the flame of our dissatisfaction in order to ask, to discover and to go further in the quest for the right to live of our heritage in its natural context; witness of a glorious past.

Galileo had said it so well: ask and they will give you, seek and you will find, knock and they will open the door for you.”

Nabatiyeh’s Heritage Day 2007

On the 25th of August 2007 APSAD was invited to participate in the program of Nabatiyeh’s Heritage Day. APSAD invited its members to share this guided visit. There were approximately 30 visitors.

The program consisted of :

►Visiting Nabatiyeh’s Municipality building.
Dr. Wehbeh told us the history of Nabatiyeh and its features..
.
►We visited the Temple of Hassan kamel El Sabbagh well Known Lebanese scientist.

►20th century old souk and houses.

►The district of the Sarail. The Sarail no longer exists. We saw there the house of Fakhreddine which was a jail for women in the days of Emir Bachir

►The district of Bayad. We visited the house of El Daher built at the end of 20th century and another one Nassar and el Chemayssani.

►We continued towards the district of the nons and visited the house of El Fadle built beginning 20th century.

►Hay el Midan - The house of El Chahine, The story tells that the grand children of this family went to Brasil to bring their old parents back to Nabatiyeh to build their houses and live there, after the first world war in 1920.

►The Greek Catholique church of As Saydeh which was demolished in the year of 2006 lately restored by the government of Qatar.

National Heritage Day - May 2006

Among APSAD’s important activities is the Heritage Day organized by the Ministry of Culture, which takes place every year the 3rd Thursday of May , since 2002. This has become a traditional day involving for the occasion , activities, free of charge, and extending over several days.

Many cultural events take place on these days,
registering a large number of visitors, and participants
– a clear indication of the growing interest of the Lebanese for their history.

APSAD has collaborated with great enthusiasm in these activities every year since their beginning.
The last National Heritage Day took place From 15 to 21 May 2006, with the collaboration of the
National Foundation of Heritage , the Association for the Protection of Old Buildings and Sites in Lebanon-APSAD-, the Saradar Foundation and Baldati.com

The program consisted of :

►Visiting the National Library with the collaboration of Saradar Foundation

►Visiting the - Old Houses in Beirut - with the collaboration of APSAD
